name: Aurnet
shortDescription: A newer UK church system with a member app, messages, people records, giving, rotas, events, pastoral care, training and a connected website.
suitableContexts: UK churches seeking a member app and public website connected to one administration platform
Teams considering a consolidated approach to communications, people records, giving and rotas
Churches prepared to pilot a recently incorporated supplier with real workflow data

pricing.summary: Aurnet advertises a free plan and a 30-day paid-plan trial, but the current public material reviewed here does not state the paid subscription prices. It states an all-in giving fee of 3.5% plus 20p per gift, including card processing; confirm the current commercial and Gift Aid terms in writing.

dataHosting: Supplier says UK data residency is a design priority and describes encrypted, tenant-isolated data. Ask for the hosting provider, exact region, data-processing agreement, sub-processors, retention and international-transfer terms.
gdprInformation: Aurnet describes itself as UK GDPR compliant and publishes a cookie policy naming Aurnet Ltd. This is a supplier claim. Before use, a church should obtain current service terms, privacy notice, DPA, sub-processor list, retention details and a workflow demonstration for pastoral and safeguarding information.

editorial.assessment: Aurnet is a broad, newly incorporated UK platform that could appeal to churches seeking one connected app, website and administration surface. Its public product scope and live iOS release make it appropriate for a cautious pilot rather than a presumption of maturity. The central decision is whether the church can validate the sensitive workflows—giving, Gift Aid, pastoral notes, safeguarding, access roles, exports and migration—before moving operational records to a new supplier.
